summary: Tested new Super Admin 'Saloni' tab and POST /api/super/tenants endpoint. 12/13 backend tests passed, all frontend flows passed including create salon, data isolation, new admin login at new slug, validation, and regular admin access control. Found 1 edge-case bug: tenant_id collision when two salons created with same name within seconds.

minor.issue: tenant_id generation can collide and return 500 (DuplicateKeyError). When two tenants are created with the same name within ~16 seconds, both produce identical tenant_id like 'tenant_test_salon_kragujeva_6a2982' because str(ObjectId())[:6] only uses ObjectId timestamp bytes. Recommendation: use uuid4().hex[:8] or full ObjectId for the suffix instead of slicing ObjectId's timestamp portion.

rca_of_the_issue: Bug: POST /api/super/tenants 500 on rapid duplicate-name creation. Root cause: routes.py:146 generates tenant_id = f'tenant_{slug.replace("-","_")[:20]}_{str(ObjectId())[:6]}'. The first 6 hex chars of an ObjectId encode the creation timestamp in seconds. Two ObjectIds generated within the same second share the same first 6 hex chars. Combined with truncated slug prefix [:20] being identical for same-name salons, the resulting tenant_id collides with the unique index 'tenant_id_1' on the tenants collection, throwing DuplicateKeyError that surfaces as 500. Reproduction: POST same name twice within 16s. Mitigation: replace str(ObjectId())[:6] with uuid.uuid4().hex[:8] or use the full str(ObjectId()) for the suffix.
